report.root_cause: At 08:45:44 an RCON client connected from 127.0.0.1 issued commands that summoned about 386 pigs (log: "[Rcon: Summoned new Pig]", all with Paper.SpawnReason COMMAND). Each pig was tagged mcsre_f, and the tag was removed at 08:45:50. The pigs also produced four junk item types at 386 each (string, rotten_flesh, stick, oak_log), about 1544 item entities in total. Entity count rose from 24 to about 1954. The RCON client that issued the summons was not identified. A new RCON session opened at 08:46:02, and no further summons were logged after 08:45:50. The TownCore heartbeat file is only a timestamp and is not the source.
report.actions: 1. Checked status and logs: TPS stayed at 20, but entities rose from 24 to 1954. 2. Searched logs: found the RCON summon burst at 08:45:44-08:45:50 and the tag removal at 08:45:50. 3. Declared the incident. 4. Inspected flood entities with console data queries: items were string, rotten_flesh, stick and oak_log at 386 each; all 387 pigs were COMMAND-spawned, none leashed or owned. 5. Identified the only named pig, Wilbur, as the 387th pig from the same run; kept it. 6. Ran "kill @e[type=minecraft:pig,name=!Wilbur]" (killed 386 pigs) and "kill @e[type=minecraft:item]" (reported 1871 killed). 7. Verified status: entities back to 24 baseline (end_crystal 10, strider 4, minecart 3, player 2, armor_stand 1, cow 1, pig 1 (Wilbur), sheep 1); TPS 20, MSPT 0.45. 8. Watched about 30 s more: no new summons, entity count stable. Did not restart the server, did not modify any file, did not ban anyone.
report.residual_risk: The source of the RCON summon burst is unknown. Anything with RCON access could repeat it, and the RCON session opened at 08:46:02 has not been identified. Wilbur was kept as a presumed non-flood pig; its ownership was not verified because protected.json could not be searched. The item kill reported 1871 entities, more than the 1544 counted earlier, so some items may have appeared between counts; the post-cleanup state matches the 24-entity baseline. Monitor for another RCON summon burst and check RCON access logs.
